newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi says Italy project investment 20 bln yen.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi says Italy project investment 20 bln yen.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp said on Tuesday that the total investment in its Italian car project with Industrie Pininfarina SpA would total 20 billion yen.

A Mitsubishi official said Mitsubishi's European unit would invest in the project to produce Mitsubishi compact sports-utility vehicles in Italy, but he did not provide a breakdown of how much each company would invest.
The total investment includes the cost of design and development, and the building of moulds and other manufacturing equipment, the official said.

Pininfarina would produce 35,000 of the vehicles a year for Mitsubishi at a Pininfarina plant in Italy. They would go on sale in the spring of 1999 through Mitsubishi's European sales network, a Mitsubishi statement said.
The vehicle's engine displacement is expected to be between 1500 cc and 2000 cc, said Hirokazu Nakamura, chairman of Mitsubishi Motors.
Under an eight-year agreement with Pininfarina, Nakamura said, Mitsubishi plans to produce a new sports-utility vehicle comparable with Toyota's RAV4 and Suzuki's sports-utility vehicle.
He said Mitsubishi hopes to take advantage of Pininfarina's design know-how in building the new vehicle.

Pininfarina group chairman Sergio Pininfarina said: "I am honoured that Mitsubishi has chosen Pininfarina for its new project." Pininfarina makes luxury and sports cars for European carmakers such as Fiat, Peugeot Citroen and Alfa-Lancia Spa.

Mitsubishi also said it is aiming to boost its European sales of Mitsubishi-brand cars to 330,000 a year by 2000, from the current 220,000. It said about half the projected sales would come from cars made in Europe.

In Europe, Mitsubishi has a Dutch unit, NedCar, owned equally by AB Volvo, Mitsubishi and the Dutch government, with an annual production capacity of 200,000 cars, producing the Volvo S40/V40, the Volvo 400 and the Mitsubishi Carisma cars.
Mitsubishi Motors president Takemune Kimura will visit Pininfarina's plant in Italy in May.
